title: Ingenol-Mediated SIRT1-LXRalpha Signaling Reduces Lipid Accumulation and Alleviates Postmenopausal Liver Damage.
authors: Liu, Meijing; Li, Shuang; Yao, Jiawei; Wang, Xiaogang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Ingenol通过SIRT1-LXRalpha信号通路缓解绝经后肝损伤，虽含分子对接但核心是脂代谢与肝损伤，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题无关。
abstract: Postmenopausal metabolic syndrome and its associated liver injury have attracted considerable research interest, yet their underlying mechanisms and treatment strategies remain insufficiently elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between aberrant lipid metabolism and hepatic injury in ovariectomized (OVX) females and to evaluate the therapeutic potential of ingenol (Ing), a natural diterpenoid, via the SIRT1-LXRalpha signaling pathway. Data from 3047 females in NHANES (2017-2020) were analyzed to compare serum triglyceride (TG) and liver injury markers between OVX and non-OVX women. An OVX mouse model was established to examine hepatic lipid metabolism and SIRT1 expression. Molecular docking, dual luciferase assays, and SIRT1 silencing were performed to evaluate Ing-SIRT1 binding and regulation. HepG2 cells were used to assess Ing's effects on lipid levels and expression of LXRalpha, CYP39A1, CPT1, and ACOX1. In vivo studies in OVX mice confirmed the therapeutic effects of Ing and further investigated its mechanism via the SIRT1-LXRalpha pathway. NHANES data indicated that OVX women had significantly higher serum TG levels and more severe liver injury. OVX mice exhibited downregulated SIRT1 expression and disrupted lipid homeostasis. Ing showed high binding affinity to SIRT1, outperforming several known agonists. In HepG2 cells, Ing reduced intracellular TG and total cholesterol (TC), while upregulating LXRalpha, CYP39A1, CPT1, and ACOX1. In OVX mice, Ing treatment notably attenuated weight gain, reduced TG and TC levels, and ameliorated liver histopathological damage. These effects were mediated through the SIRT1-LXRalpha pathway. Ing effectively mitigates OVX-induced liver injury by activating SIRT1 and modulating downstream LXRalpha-mediated lipid metabolic pathways. These results support Ing as a promising therapeutic candidate for liver injury in postmenopausal or OVX women.
abstract_zh: 绝经后代谢综合征及其相关肝损伤已引起广泛研究关注，但其潜在机制和治疗策略仍未得到充分阐明。本研究旨在探讨去卵巢（OVX）雌性中异常脂质代谢与肝损伤之间的关系，并评估天然二萜类化合物巨大戟醇（Ing）通过SIRT1-LXRalpha信号通路的治疗潜力。分析了NHANES（2017-2020）中3047名女性的数据，比较OVX与非OVX女性的血清甘油三酯（TG）和肝损伤标志物。建立了OVX小鼠模型以检查肝脏脂质代谢和SIRT1表达。进行了分子对接、双荧光素酶实验和SIRT1沉默，以评估Ing与SIRT1的结合及调控。使用HepG2细胞评估Ing对脂质水平及LXRalpha、CYP39A1、CPT1和ACOX1表达的影响。OVX小鼠的体内研究证实了Ing的治疗效果，并进一步通过SIRT1-LXRalpha通路探讨了其机制。NHANES数据表明，OVX女性的血清TG水平显著更高，肝损伤更严重。OVX小鼠表现出SIRT1表达下调和脂质稳态紊乱。Ing对SIRT1显示出高结合亲和力，优于几种已知激动剂。在HepG2细胞中，Ing降低了细胞内TG和总胆固醇（TC），同时上调了LXRalpha、CYP39A1、CPT1和ACOX1。在OVX小鼠中，Ing治疗显著减轻了体重增加，降低了TG和TC水平，并改善了肝脏组织病理学损伤。这些效应通过SIRT1-LXRalpha通路介导。Ing通过激活SIRT1并调节下游LXRalpha介导的脂质代谢通路，有效缓解OVX诱导的肝损伤。这些结果支持Ing作为绝经后或OVX女性肝损伤的有前景的治疗候选药物。
